question: Your CI pipeline runs Claude Code with the -p flag and --json-schema to generate test cases for each pull request and to record the acceptance criteria that each test covers. A validation step rejects bad outputs and retries up to three times, appending the specific validation errors to the prompt. Outputs with misnamed fields pass on the first retry. Outputs with an empty acceptance criteria field still fail after all three retries, and those pull request descriptions say only "criteria in the design doc," a file the pipeline never passes to Claude Code. What is the most likely reason these retries keep failing?

options.text: The limit of three retries is too low, because Claude Code needs more attempts to locate the criteria inside the pull request description.
options.reason: The criteria are absent from the pull request description, so extra attempts cannot find them; retries help only with format or structural errors.

options.text: The acceptance criteria exist only in the design document, which the pipeline never provides, so no retry can produce them from the pull request.
options.reason: Retries are ineffective when the required information is absent from the source, as it is when the information exists only in an external document that is never provided.

options.text: The JSON schema lacks strict mode, so syntax errors in the generated output keep clearing the acceptance criteria field on each attempt.
options.reason: Schema syntax errors are a separate problem that strict schemas and tool use eliminate, and the failing field is empty because the source lacks the information.

options.text: The appended validation errors are too vague to guide Claude Code toward the criteria, so the error messages need more detail about the expected values.
options.reason: The same specific error feedback fixed the misnamed fields, and no error message can make Claude Code produce criteria that are absent from its input.
